questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was drawn to Edinburgh because of its interesting history and the beautiful nature surrounding the city. I was also aware that they provide excellent opportunities for students to socialize through various student societies.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university webside was pretty easy to navigate and they always replied very quickly to inquiries but the process of applying for exchange (anywhere) is overall very confusing and bureaucratic.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Due to Covid the social activities in the welcome week were limited but there were still a bunch of social things to do. I would recommend to sign up for these things as quickly as possible, through the Student Association webpage, because lots of the events sell out fast. Even though I wasn't aware of this I still had lots of things to do - there are also a lot of private initiatives from other new students who are also eager to meet new people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not that easy. I did a post on Facebook in a group for new international students in Edinburgh and then found a longterm Airbnb rental with 2 other exchange students in Haymarket.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I preferred this option because I heard from others that dorms were for younger students who didn't have much experience living on their own. I think you have more freedom living off campus where you can choose your roommates yourself. At least that was my experience :)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I applied for three courses (30 ETCS) but only two were available so I had to sign up for another one, which was then approved. I did however end up changing 2 out of 3 within the two first weeks of the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international student office is very helpful and quick at replying.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't get the classes that I wanted at first but your assigned at personal tutor after the Welcome Week who's very helpful with getting you into the right classes. My experience was that they were very flexible when it came to changing courses and that most people got the courses they wanted in the end.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the University page "Path" when you've gotten your university login to put together your time schedule - it's very helpful

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did two year 1 courses and one year 3 course

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I really liked the teachers pedagogical style. Most of my professors were good at engaging us. I also loved having tutorials/seminars after every lecture where we'd discuss that week's curriculum and attach it to concrete examples.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sustainable Development 1a: Introducing Sustainable Development
Scottish Studies: Conceptualizing Scotland 
Educational Politics & Policy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The course "Sustainable Development 1a: Introducing Sustainable Development"
If you're interested in Climate and sustainability the courses adresses some of the biggest challenges right now. The teacher's are very engaged in the topic and it provides a wide overview of the issue from different perspectives (anthropological, phycological, political, geografical, anti-capitalist and so on).

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I spent quite a lot of money on trip with the Hillwalking society - completely worth it though!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and beer (tennants) is cheaper than Denmark but housing is very expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There's a society for pretty much anything facilitated by the student association union

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Hillwalking society! 
I also enjoyed the Water of Life society (whisky society) and the sociology society

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Definitely go to Glasgow. I was there at least 5 times.
Go on trips to the Highland, the islands, St Andrews and such
Or go to Arthur's Seat, the Pendlands and experience the beautiful nature Edinburgh provides

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Edinburgh is a very international city with lots of students and therefore very easy to integrate into

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Societies!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Can't think of any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Their pub culture with cheap beer and live music
Also go to a Ceilidh if you get the chance - it's very scottish and a lot of fun!
Scots are very easy to talk to and very outgoing and polite, which makes it easy to talk to people and feel welcomed

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open to try new things even though it might seem overwhelming and awkward at first
Don't hold back with your money - take a SU loan if necessary - you'll regret it overwise
But also say learn when to say no to things if you're feeling stressed out and drained from energy

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember that you can change your courses until two weeks into the semester

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to discuss the content of my courses with my fellow students and professor in tutorials. It really improved my English skills and made me very engaged in the course. I wish we could do this more in Denmark.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I missed my boyfriend a lot and missed having a study group when writing exams - they were all individual.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
